payload.claim: `_finish_verify.verify` exports `.saffron/` for the finishing suite from `pinned.base_sha`, the sha pinned once at batch start (`cli.py:1525-1526`) and never refreshed. `package_phase.reverify`'s own established caller, PACKAGE, deliberately does the opposite: it re-fetches the default branch's live head (`fetch_default_branch`, `package.py:675`) right before exporting gates, with a comment explaining why (`package.py:710-714`) — verifying against a stale declaration would judge a pull request under rules that no longer govern. A `--stack` batch can run for hours; if `.saffron/policy.yaml` or a gate script changes on the default branch during that night, the finishing layer's own pull request is judged against the policy as it stood at batch start, not as it stands when the finishing suite actually runs and the PR opens. No test in this diff exercises a policy/gates change between batch start and finish, so this drift is invisible to the suite that passed.
